trick: The theories fall into two families and the names say which. Nebular and Planetesimal are 'the sun had help from another body or a cloud'; the Big Bang is the origin of the universe, not of the earth alone. Kant and Laplace go with nebular; Chamberlin and Moulton with planetesimal; Jeans and Jeffreys with the tidal theory.

trick: The waves prove the structure. P-waves travel through solids and liquids; S-waves cannot pass through liquid at all — and that single fact is how we know the outer core is molten. The shadow zone on the far side of the earth is the evidence you can point to.

chapter: Atmosphere: Insolation, Pressure and the Greenhouse Effect
trick: Incoming solar radiation is short-wave and passes through the atmosphere easily; the heat the earth radiates back is long-wave and gets trapped. That asymmetry IS the greenhouse effect. Also remember the atmosphere is heated from below, by the earth, not directly by the sun — which is why it gets colder as you climb.

data.prompt: True or false? Mark each statement about the atmosphere.

items.statement: The lower atmosphere is heated mainly by radiation from the earth's surface, not directly by the sun.
items.why: Short-wave solar radiation passes through; the ground absorbs it and re-radiates long-wave heat, which the air absorbs. Hence the fall in temperature with height.

items.statement: Insolation is greatest at the equator and least at the poles.
items.why: The sun's rays are near vertical at the equator and slanting at the poles, spreading the same energy over a larger area.
It decreases — there is less air above you. This is why aircraft cabins are pressurised.

items.statement: The troposphere is the layer where all weather occurs.
items.why: It holds almost all the water vapour and dust, and its temperature falls with height, allowing convection.
They let short-wave radiation in and hold long-wave radiation on the way out. Blocking sunlight would cool the earth, not warm it.

items.statement: The normal lapse rate is about 6.5 °C per kilometre.
items.why: It is the standard figure for the fall of temperature with height in the troposphere.
